findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables block, committing long-lived credentials to source control and exposing them to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or console read access.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable in cleartext by any principal with function read permissions; a customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy is required for defence in depth.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet boundary, easing data exfiltration if the function is compromised.

The trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, permitting any Lambda function in the service principal's scope rather than constraining assumption to this specific function/account.
